paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: What are the qualities of the form realm? We're going to go through things a bit quickly now. So, the form realm — one quality is that it's beyond the desire realm. The only thing we're going to say about it right now is this: what exists in the form realm are the kinds of objects that the beings there would experience as creating mental afflictions. Just as all the objects in our desire realm have the possibility of creating a non-virtuous action, there are particular kinds of things in the form realm that do that for the beings who are there, and they accumulate non-virtue.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: But why is it called the form realm? Because form — suk [GZUGS] — reaches its highest expression there. The beings there have beautiful bodies — not "kind of," they do. Their form, their appearance, reaches a kind of ultimate beauty — the most perfect of perfect. There's a problem, though: when everything is so perfect, you have no motivation to do anything except enjoy the perfection. And it's not really perfect, because they die too. We'll talk about it. But just imagine Marvel superheroes, or what we would consider god-like beings — they're not enlightened, but they have that kind of quality.

chapters.title: The Levels of the Form Realm

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Okay, what are these four people doing? Just write this down — it's boring information, but write it down. The form realm has four different levels; that's why there are four people here. The first three levels each have three different levels within them, for a total of nine. The fourth one has eight sections, for a total of seventeen.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: I watched this funny video the other day. The person said, "so there are three levels of three levels, and then eight more — how many is that?" I'm changing the details, but you get it. And immediately the other person said, "seventeen." And the one who asked said, "how did you type that into Claude so fast?" And she said, "I have ChatGPT in my head." And the guy goes, "oh, is there a new implant? How do I get that chip?" And she says, "oh, I'll show you" — and she writes out the math on a piece of paper and says, "that's my ChatGPT." And he's like, "wow."

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: So please don't rely on those things — use your brain, use your neurons. Nine plus eight: don't reach for a calculator. So there are 17 levels in the form realm. And each one has a cause — a particular type of meditation. Don't worry, most of you don't even have good enough meditation to get there; you already have to have shamatha, and more.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: One more thing, and then we're almost done. There's a level called ok-min ['OG MIN], and it means "below none." Is ok-min part of the form realm or not? It's just a terminology question — because there's also a Buddha paradise called ok-min ['OG MIN], which is this next slide, tukpo köpa ['OG MIN STUG PO BKOD PA]. So basically, there are two places with essentially the same name: a Buddha paradise called this, and one of the four form-realm levels also called ok-min. That's for the nerds out there — I wouldn't even have said it, except it's a homework question, so I feel compelled.

chapters.title: Your World Comes From How You Treated Others

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: So, the last point for today — which we've already talked about. What makes for your world? The Abhidharma is going to talk about all the different types of worlds there are. But the world you live in is defined by how you treated other people in the past. Every single thing around you is like a blank screen — including United Airlines' dessert cart. Some people eat that dessert and become the sexiest muscle-bound bodybuilder alive; others eat it and go, "oh, my stomach hurts, why did I just eat that ice cream?"

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Every single object in the universe has emptiness. And what you see is forced upon you by how you treated others in the past — whether that ice cream creates sexiness or an uncomfortable stomach. And even more than that: it may not even be food for everybody. It could be poison. It could be deathless nectar. It could be the source of every single bliss in your life. But it all depends on how you treated other people in the past. For now, I should avoid the sundae — but if I had different seeds... and that's a practice.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: But every single being you see, every life form, everything you see in this universe, is coming from how you treated other people in the past. And then, when you reach death, and you're pushing through the veil of your next life — what being is going to go through? What throwing karma — the kind of karma that throws a next life — what collection of karmas is going to open up in that moment? And much of it depends on how you took care of yourself and others in this life: how well you took care of your mind, and your heart, and the hearts of others.

chapters.title: This Week's Meditations — and Working With Your Teacher

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: So that's what we're going to talk about in this class. The meditations we're going to do this week are not the meditations of Classics Course 8 — you can do those in your study groups. We're going to focus on the preparation meditations that Geshe Michael has been giving for the transmission in October, which are all about understanding what seeds brought you into this life. Can we use logic to understand what came before that created this time?

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: We're going to review some of the meditations we did in July in Malaysia, and Brian and I are going to give new ones you haven't seen yet. Normally we keep those meditations for the 30-30-30 program — the big fundraiser that keeps ACI running — but I think these meditations are too important to hold off for a couple of months, so we're going to practice them this week too.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: One of the advantages of living in Sedona is that we have weekly meditations with Geshe Michael. And I decided that if I want to keep having those private meditations, then we should also share them with all of you this week. And I got permission from Geshe Michael, too — I didn't do it without permission. That's a requirement in the Diamond Way: you always have to ask the teacher first. You ask the teacher to do things.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: And it's not what you think it is, either. Don't ask me if you can go to the bathroom — I do not want to be fielding questions like that. You're a big boy, you're a big girl; you can do a lot of things on your own. And part of being a practitioner is learning how to do things on your own, including your practice — and learning when it's appropriate to ask your teacher for advice and guidance, and when it's inappropriate. It's an art form. And every teacher's standard is different; and if you want to get even more subtle, your teacher is in a different state every time they meet with you. Why? Exactly — because it's all coming from you anyway.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: If you don't think like that, you will not have a successful practice. Every success, and every difficulty you have in that relationship, is coming from you. Because this is how we think: when things are great, it's coming from you — "that's my doing." When you're having a challenging time with them, it's coming from them, because they're acting like assholes, right? But in the Diamond Way practice, you have to, you have to, you have to, you have to understand that it's coming from you. The relationship you have is coming from you, and whatever comes up is coming from you. The more you can understand that, the more you can navigate it.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: And the fact that you have a teacher in your life — you should celebrate, because you must have done something good. Even if they piss you off. But you have to deal with it. And you don't deal with it with them — the relationship is your responsibility. Don't make it their fault; otherwise you're just projecting your mommy and daddy issues. The teacher will keep testing you. And that test is coming from you too, anyway.
